task: Verify that the Java Margo project driver runs real tests and benchmarks rather than placeholder success output.
observation: The Java ProjectBuilder test and bench commands discovered project files but then emitted hard-coded PASS and benchmark records without evaluating any Moss declarations. Existing phase7 project fixtures made this visible: one intentionally failing test was reported as passing, and benchmark output did not depend on project declarations.
impact: A green project command gave no correctness evidence and could mask failing package tests. Implementing declaration discovery and execution with the Java Fast Debug interpreter made the passing and intentional-failure fixtures report their actual outcomes; benchmarks now execute declared bodies and report measured samples.

resolution.summary: Project test and bench commands now select, type-check, execute, and report discovered Moss bodies. Project tests currently use Fast Debug and project benchmarks measure Fast Debug interpreter execution; native test and benchmark parity remain part of candidate acceptance.

task: Preserve complete exported enum payload shapes in Java module metadata.
observation: The Java project metadata writer serialized only the first field of each enum case in both ABI-v9 contract output and ABI-v10 binary records. The C++ v9 writer emits every field, and the ABI-v9 reader consumes a field count followed by every name/type pair. Java now serializes all enum fields in ABI-v9 contract and semantic-export rows and in ABI-v10 binary enum records.
impact: Truncating payload fields loses source-free enum type information. The change closes the serialization defect for the encodings it touches; ABI-v10 semantic enum records and full source-free loading remain unimplemented.
evidence: ./scripts/java/test.sh passed all eight test classes, including three-field contract and semantic record serialization

resolution.summary: Enum field iteration now preserves complete payload arity in ABI-v9 contract and semantic-export sections and ABI-v10 binary records. Full source-free module acceptance remains open.

task: Use the canonical ABI-v10 codec during source-free provider validation.
observation: The Margo validator checked the v10 outer digest and provider marker but did not invoke the existing CheckedBodyCodec verifier. It now verifies canonical sections, framing, ordering, section hashes, interface re-encoding, and checked-body hashes before accepting an artifact. The Java v10 writer sorts record sections and imports to match canonical encoding.
impact: A valid outer digest alone does not authenticate ABI-v10 section semantics. Reusing the canonical codec closes that validation gap for containers it can decode; incomplete logical records and noncanonical dependency module IDs remain open in the writer.
evidence: ProjectBuilderMetadataTest recomputes the outer digest after corrupting the section hash and confirms SOURCE_FREE_CONTRACT_INVALID

resolution.summary: V10 source-free validation now reuses CheckedBodyCodec verification; writer record ordering is canonicalized. Full semantic record validation remains incomplete.

task: Bind ABI-v10 import records to the selected provider's actual module identity and contract hashes.
observation: The Java ABI-v10 writer previously emitted short dependency names and copied the outer provider digest into both binary and semantic contract hash slots. It now uses the selected dependency .mossi module ID and its distinct v10 binary and semantic hashes, and fails closed when they are absent.
impact: Import records must bind the actual selected provider and both independent contracts. Reusing an outer digest creates invalid v10 import metadata and can hide a mismatched dependency contract.
evidence: ProjectBuilderMetadataTest covers correctly bound imports and rejects a missing binary contract hash

resolution.summary: The v10 import writer now emits complete provider identity/hash rows and requests a v10 rebuild for incomplete dependencies. Full v10 source-free semantics remain open.

task: Emit and load ABI-v9 exported function signatures and generic body facts.
observation: Java ABI-v9 function records previously omitted return/parameter signatures and generic body records. The loader silently ignored malformed parse exceptions and dropped generic call arguments and result expressions. The writer now emits exported function records and generic body fields; the reader preserves arguments/results, syncs the native alias, and surfaces malformed metadata.
impact: Source-free consumers need callable signatures and semantic bodies to specialize generic helpers. This improves record coverage but is not safe full ABI-v9 support because parameter access is currently serialized as READ and function/method effects remain approximate.
evidence: SourceFreeFunctionMetadataTest verifies generic parameter, dispatch, statement arguments, result expression, and alias synchronization

resolution.summary: Function type/body records and loader coverage improved; accurate access/effect derivation and native source-free integration remain open.
